title: Frontend Developer
tagline: Build the interfaces people see, touch and love: fast, accessible and beautiful.
about: Frontend developers turn designs and product ideas into the part of software that people actually use. You work in the browser with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, usually through a framework like React, and you care about speed, accessibility and feel.
It's one of the most visible jobs in tech and one of the best entry points: you can see your progress on screen from day one.
day: Build UI components from designs in Figma
Fetch data from APIs and manage state
Make pages fast, responsive and accessible
Write tests and review teammates' pull requests
Debug layout and performance issues in DevTools

phases.title: Web foundations
phases.goal: Build and style static pages with semantic HTML and modern CSS.

nodes.d: What happens between typing a URL and seeing a page: DNS, HTTP requests, servers and the browser's rendering pipeline.
Structure content with the right elements so it works for screen readers, search engines and other developers.
Selectors, the cascade, specificity and the box model: the rules that decide how everything looks.
The two modern layout systems. Flexbox for one dimension, Grid for two.
links: CSS-Tricks: A complete guide to Flexbox
CSS-Tricks: A complete guide to CSS Grid

nodes.d: Pages that work on every screen size, designed mobile-first.
About 1 in 6 people has a disability. Accessible sites work with keyboards and screen readers and are legally required in many places.
Track every change and publish your work.

project.d: A multi-section personal site using semantic HTML, Grid and Flexbox, with a working mobile layout and an accessibility score of 100 in Lighthouse. Deploy it to GitHub Pages.

phases.title: JavaScript in depth
phases.goal: Program the browser: logic, the DOM, events and asynchronous code.

nodes.d: Values, types, functions, objects, arrays and modern syntax: the core language before any framework.
Find elements, change them, and react to clicks, input and keyboard events.
The event loop, callbacks, promises and async/await. Essential for anything that talks to a server.
Load JSON from REST APIs with fetch, show loading and error states, and handle CORS.
Persist data in the browser and know which store fits.
Inspect elements, debug JavaScript with breakpoints and profile performance.

project.t: Interactive web app without a framework
project.d: Build a weather or movie-search app in plain JavaScript that calls a public API, handles loading and errors, and saves favourites to localStorage.

phases.title: TypeScript & a framework
phases.goal: Build component-based apps with React and catch bugs at compile time with TypeScript.

nodes.d: Types make large codebases safer and editors smarter. Nearly every modern frontend job uses it.
Components, props and state: describing UI as a function of data.
Effects, refs, context and custom hooks, and knowing when not to use effects.
Multi-page apps with client-side routing, and data libraries that cache and revalidate.
Bundlers, dev servers and package managers turn your source into fast production assets.
Know what Vue, Svelte and Angular trade off so you can read them and choose sensibly.

project.d: A typed React app (for example a habit tracker or kanban board) with routing, persistent data, form validation and a polished responsive UI.

phases.title: Professional frontend
phases.goal: Ship production-quality code: tested, styled at scale, fast and server-rendered.

nodes.d: Approaches that keep CSS maintainable in big apps, and design tokens that keep UIs consistent.
Unit tests for logic, component tests for behaviour and end-to-end tests for critical flows.
Load fast and stay responsive. Measure first with real metrics.
Render on the server for speed and SEO, with routing and data fetching built in.
The browser's attack surface: XSS, CSRF and the headers that defend against them.
Get apps online with previews for every pull request.

project.d: A Next.js app with authentication, a real backend or BaaS, 90+ Lighthouse scores, tests in CI and a preview deploy per pull request. Write a case study for your portfolio.

phases.title: Senior skills
phases.goal: Grow from building features to owning frontends.

nodes.d: Reusable, documented, accessible components shared across teams.
Choose where state lives: server cache, URL, local, global, and keep it simple.
How rendering, layout, paint and compositing work, so you can reason about jank.

nodes.t: Reading and contributing to open source
nodes.d: Read real codebases and send your first pull requests.
links: The Architecture of Open Source Applications

interview: Explain the box model, specificity and how Flexbox and Grid differ.
Event loop questions: predict the order of logs with promises and setTimeout.
Build a component live (autocomplete, modal, infinite list) with accessibility in mind.
Explain how React renders and when components re-render.
Easy and medium algorithm problems on arrays, strings and hash maps.
certs: freeCodeCamp Responsive Web Design and JavaScript certifications
